sec.title: Definition
sec.p: A recombinant haploid tree process is a stochastic process, which has an underlying probability space (\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P) (Ω,ℱ,P), along with the following underlying fixed givens:

list-item.p: a time function, denoted \mathrm{At} At, mapping \mathrm{Haps} Haps to \Re ℜ,
a set of real times \mathrm{Time}\subset \Re Time⊂ℜ.

sec.p: Depending on the application, potential haploids might be interpreted as potential organisms, gametes, or spores.

sec.title: Haploid lineages
sec.p: A haploid lineage represents all the haploids transmitting genetic information at a genomic locus to a descendant haploid.
Formally, a haploid lineage is a set of haploids, L \subset \mathrm{Haps} L⊂Haps, such that, with the ordering induced by \mathrm{At} At, L L is

list-item.p: every subset of L L has a maximum (newest) haploid.

sec.p: The maximum (newest) haploid in a haploid lineage L L is denoted \mathrm{Tip}(L) Tip(L). Let \mathrm{Pred}(\ell, h) Pred(ℓ,h) denote \mathrm{Tip}(\mathrm{Lin}(\ell, h) / \{h\}) Tip(Lin(ℓ,h)/{h}), that is, the predecessor haploid of h h from which genetic information was copied at locus \ell ℓ.

For any haploid lineage L \in \mathrm{Haplins} L∈Haplins, a subset S \subset L S⊂L is a sublineage of L L iff
\forall x \in L, y \in S: \mathrm{At}(x) < \mathrm{At}(y) \implies x \in S \text{ .} ∀x∈L,y∈S:At(x)<At(y)⟹x∈S .
For convenience, let \mathrm{At}(L) = \mathrm{At}(\mathrm{Tip}(L)) At(L)=At(Tip(L)) for any lineage L L.

sec.p: A set of haploid lineages T \subset \mathrm{Haplins} T⊂Haplins is a haploid tree iff for every member lineage L \in T L∈T, every sublineage of L L is also a member of T T.

The union of a haploid tree T T is the union of all its member lineages is denoted
\bigcup T ⋃T.

sec.p: The Kingman n n-coalescent1 is defined as a stochastic process terminating at a sample of haploids. As a time-indexed random variable, the n n-coalescent takes values as equivalence relations (partitions) on the samples.

Given a fixed locus \ell \in \mathrm{Loci} ℓ∈Loci, and a sample population S \subset \mathrm{Haps} S⊂Haps, where for some time z \in Time z∈Time, for all a \in S a∈S, z = At(a) z=At(a), a recombinant haploid tree process defines a backward-time-indexed random variable X_r Xr that takes the same values as the Kingman n n-coalescent, but not necessarily with the same probability distribution. sec.title: King genealogy tree processes
sec.p:
King2 extends the genealogical tree structure of the Kingman
n n-coalescent, but with some differences:

list-item.p: samples need not be at the same time,
partitions are used instead of equivalence relations,
time is indexed forwards, not backwards, and
time zero is fixed to the root of the genealogical tree.

sec.title: Ancestral Recombination Graph (ARG)
sec.p: An ancestral recombination graph3 45 of a sampled population is embedded in any outcome of any recombinant haploid lineage process. We formally show the exact embedding using the gARG formalism6.
This genetic legacy is the genetic material that survives in the sample population S S originally copied from ancestral haploid h h (with or without mutations).

Genetic legacy for a sample population S S induces the following equivalence relation over pairs of haploids h_1 h1 and h_2 h2 in
\mathrm{Haps} Haps:
h_1 \simeq_S h_2 \ := \ \mathrm{Legacy}(h_1, S) = \mathrm{Legacy}(h_2, S) \text{ .} h1≃Sh2:=Legacy(h1,S)=Legacy(h2,S) . We denote the resulting equivalence class containing h \in \mathrm{Haps} h∈Haps as
{[h]}_S \ := \ \{ h' : \mathrm{Legacy}(h', S) = \mathrm{Legacy}(h, S) \} \text{ .} [h]S:={h′:Legacy(h′,S)=Legacy(h,S)} .
In this equivalence relation, haploids are considered equivalent if they have the same genetic legacy for the sample population S S.

The (unannotated) graph edges of the gARG are chosen as child-parent node pairs (C, P) \in \mathrm{Nodes}(S)^2 (C,P)∈Nodes(S)2 where
\mathrm{Pred}(\ell, h) \in P \text{ for some $h \in C$ and some $\ell \in \mathrm{Loci}$ .} Pred(ℓ,h)∈P for some h∈C and some ℓ∈Loci .

In the gARG, annotations are added for each graph edge (pair of child and parent nodes). This annotation is the set of locations through which genetic information has been copied from parent to child. In the following interpretation, the only locations of interest are those for which genetic information has been transmitted into the sample population S S. With this interpretation, the annotation for edge
(C,P) (C,P) is
\{ \ell \in \mathrm{Loci}: C \subseteq \mathrm{Lin}(\ell, h) \text{ and } P \subseteq \mathrm{Lin}(\ell, h) \text{ for some $h \in S$} \} \text{ .} {ℓ∈Loci:C⊆Lin(ℓ,h) and P⊆Lin(ℓ,h) for some h∈S} .
